content.title: About
content.content: Feta is a traditional Greek cheese made from whole milk (usually cow, sheep or goat), sold in crumbled form. It has a characteristic salty, slightly tangy flavor and a crumbly yet firm texture. Feta is widely used in salads, appetizers and Mediterranean dishes.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Feta is considered one of the oldest cheeses in the world; it is mentioned in ancient Greek texts.
Traditionally feta is made from sheep’s or goat’s milk, but modern industrial versions often include whole cow’s milk.
According to the EU, only cheese produced in Greece following the traditional recipe can be called “feta”.
Feta is stored in brine, which gives it its salty taste and extends its shelf life.
Crumbled feta is convenient for sprinkling over dishes because it distributes quickly.

items.title: Rich source of calcium
items.content: Feta provides a notable amount of calcium, which supports bone and tooth health.

items.title: High in protein
items.content: Protein in feta helps maintain muscle mass and promotes satiety.

items.title: Contains probiotics
items.content: The fermentation process creates beneficial bacteria that support gut microbiota.

items.title: Low lactose content
items.content: Fermentation reduces lactose levels, making feta more tolerable for people with mild lactose intolerance.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Feta supplies vitamins B2 and B12, important for energy metabolism and nervous system function.

items.title: High sodium
items.content: Because feta is stored in brine, it can contribute a significant amount of sodium if consumed in large quantities.

items.title: Milk protein allergy
items.content: As a dairy product, feta may trigger allergic reactions in individuals sensitive to casein.

items.title: Fat content
items.content: Whole‑milk feta contains saturated fats; people monitoring cholesterol should eat it in moderation.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Crumbled feta is perfect for sprinkling over salads, pastas, casseroles and pizza. It can be added to omelets, vegetable stews, or used as a filling for pies. For a softer texture, gently mash feta with a fork.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep feta in its original brine in an airtight container in the refrigerator at 1‑4 °C. If needed, transfer to fresh brine (water + salt). It lasts 2‑3 weeks. Discard if it develops an off‑odor or discoloration.
